cohort: The study included 40 HIV-positive pregnant women (with 45 parities) aged 18 or older, matched with 45 HIV-negative pregnant women (parities) as controls, with data collected between 2011 and 2018.
finding: HIV-positive women were found to deliver fetuses with lower body weight and had higher rates of preterm delivery and small-for-gestational age, but no vertical transmission of HIV was observed.
mod_finding: Mild perineal lacerations were observed in HIV-positive women who delivered via normal spontaneous delivery (NSD), but no other specific findings related to mode of birth were detailed as the groups were matched for delivery method.
birth_weight: The mean birth weight was 2665g for HIV- and ART-exposed fetuses, compared to 3010g for controls.
gest_age: The study reported higher rates of preterm delivery (28.9% vs 8.9%) and small-for-gestational-age (28.9% vs 8.8%) in the HIV-positive group.
